pairs.registryProposal: Lexical matching tied this context to authorization through 'audit'/'review', but the governing fact is something else: a TS IPC-wrapper context exposes operations whose tiers are declared in Rust, so the verdict has to be anchored in the Rust command files. The registry could say in an application note that for an IPC-client context the authorization pair is judged over the commands it invokes, not over the wrapper files. Upward lesson: this repo shows a partial-adoption shape the technique does not name - a declarative macro (#[requires]) beside a hand-written guard of the same name (require_auth_sync) that has become a no-op. A reader sees a guard on every command, and in this context 414 of 422 of them enforce nothing. declarative-requirements could name the 'vestigial guard call' as a failure mode alongside the dual-artifact drift.
